jeongsi2027.title: 2027 Regular Admission Schedule (Korea)
jeongsi2027.subtitle: From CSAT score release to regular applications, group A/B/C screening, results, registration and additional recruitment, with a D-day count from today.

top.staticSub: Each university takes applications on at least 3 of these days
top.tipBefore: Focus on your condition until the CSAT. If you are aiming for regular admission, use your self-scored results right after the exam to see which universities are within reach.
top.tipDone: Early, regular and additional rounds for 2027 are all over. The next year's schedule will be added once KCUE announces it.

csat.name: CSAT exam day
csat.note: Based on KICE's 2027 CSAT administration plan (announced March 31, 2026).
csat.tip: Use your self-scored results to gauge your regular admission range, and keep track of any remaining early admission exams. Scores come out on December 11.

score.name: CSAT score release
score.note: Score reports reach test takers on this day, with standard scores, percentiles and grades.
score.tip: Convert your standard scores and percentiles with each university's formula and shortlist candidates for each group. Early admission results are due by December 18.

susiResult.name: Early admission results
susiResult.note: First-round early admission results are announced by this date. If you are admitted, you cannot apply in the regular or additional rounds, even without registering.
susiResult.tip: If you were admitted in early admission, including from the waitlist, you cannot apply in the regular round whether or not you register. If you have several offers, choose the one to register at.

susiReg.name: Early admission registration
susiReg.note: Admitted early applicants register at one university only within these 3 days (document registration or deposit).
susiReg.tip: Early admission registration at a single university closes December 23. If you are preparing for regular admission, check each target university's guide for dates and score weighting.

susiExtra.name: Early admission waitlist offers
susiExtra.note: Unfilled seats go to waitlisted applicants in order. Website announcements run until 2 p.m.; from 2 to 6 p.m. offers are made individually, for example by phone.
susiExtra.tip: Waitlist offers are going out. If you are on a waitlist, answer your phone. A waitlist admission still counts as admission, so you cannot apply in the regular round.

susiExtraReg.name: Early waitlist registration
susiExtraReg.note: Registration deadline for early admission waitlist offers. The early round ends on this day.
susiExtraReg.tip: The early round is over. Sign up for an integrated account with an application service (UWAY Apply or Jinhak Apply) and fill in the common application and refund account in advance.

apply.name: Regular admission applications
apply.note: Each university takes applications on at least 3 of these days, and closing dates and times differ by university. You can apply to up to 3 universities, one per group.
apply.tip: This is the application window and the days right after it. Check each university's closing time and apply early; once done, check your receipt with the exam number and the group A exam schedule.

groupA.name: Group A screening
groupA.note: Seven days when group A universities hold interviews, practical exams and other screening. Check the exact dates and times in each admission guide.
groupA.tip: Group A interviews and practical exams take place this week. Double-check the venue, time and what to bring in the admission guide.

groupB.name: Group B screening
groupB.note: Seven days when group B universities hold interviews, practical exams and other screening. Check the exact dates and times in each admission guide.
groupB.tip: Group B interviews and practical exams take place this week. Double-check the venue, time and what to bring in the admission guide.

groupC.name: Group C screening
groupC.note: Seven days when group C universities hold interviews, practical exams and other screening. Check the exact dates and times in each admission guide.
groupC.tip: Group C screening runs until January 31, and universities announce results by February 5. Note each announcement time and how to check it.

result.name: Regular admission results
result.note: Deadline for first-round results. Universities may announce earlier, so check the announcement date in each guide.
result.tip: First-round results are out. If you have several offers, register at only one during February 10–12, and check your waitlist rank too.

reg.name: Regular admission registration
reg.note: Pay tuition and register at only one of the universities that admitted you. Closing times differ by university (e.g., Korea University: February 12, 2 p.m.).
reg.tip: Registration is open. Closing times differ, so check yours and register at one university only. Not registering in time counts as declining.

extra.name: Regular waitlist offers
extra.note: Unfilled seats go to waitlisted applicants in order. Website announcements run until 2 p.m.; from 2 to 6 p.m. offers are made individually, for example by phone.
extra.tip: Waitlist offers are going out. To switch universities, withdraw your registration at the first university before registering at the new one.

extraReg.name: Regular waitlist registration
extraReg.note: Registration deadline for regular waitlist offers. To apply for additional recruitment, you must withdraw your regular registration by 4 p.m. on this day.
extraReg.tip: Today is the regular waitlist registration deadline. To apply for additional recruitment, withdraw your regular registration by 4 p.m. Additional recruitment notices appear after 6 p.m.

addRecruit.name: Additional recruitment
addRecruit.note: Universities fill seats left after the regular round. Applications, offers (by 6 p.m. on the 26th) and registration (by 10 p.m. on the 26th) all happen within 8 days.
addRecruit.tip: Additional recruitment runs until February 26. Applications and announcements move quickly, so check notices as soon as they are posted.

timeline.title: 2027 university admission schedule
timeline.desc: The common KCUE schedule from the CSAT to additional recruitment. Tap a calendar button to download an event with a reminder 3 days before.
timeline.note: This is the common KCUE schedule; actual application, announcement and registration times differ by university. Each university's admission guide takes precedence.

rules.title: Regular admission rules
items: You can apply to up to 3 universities, one in each of groups A, B and C. Applying to two or more in the same group (including departments of the same university in the same group) voids your admission.
If you were admitted in early admission (first round or waitlist), you cannot apply in the regular or additional rounds, even if you did not register.
Even with several offers, you may register at only one university (no double registration). Violations lead to cancelled admission.
Anyone registered in the regular round cannot apply for additional recruitment, unless they withdraw by 4 p.m. on the regular waitlist registration deadline (February 18).

Industrial universities and junior colleges have no group limit. The multiple-application and double-registration bans do not apply between regular universities and special-act institutions such as the military academies, Korean National Police University, KAIST and Korea National University of Arts.
Once submitted (an exam number is issued), an application cannot be cancelled and the fee is generally non-refundable.
rules.warn: January 4–7 is the common window set by KCUE. Actual application days (at least 3 of these) and closing times differ by university. For example, Korea University (Seoul) accepts applications from January 4, 10 a.m. to January 6, 6 p.m. Always check your target university's admission guide.

adiga.name: Adiga admission portal
adiga.desc: Run by KCUE. Admission guides and past results for each university.

share.text: {headline} · 2027 regular admission applications, group A/B/C, results and additional recruitment at a glance

groups.title: What are groups A, B and C (Ga, Na, Da)?
items: The regular screening period is split into group A (January 11–17), group B (January 18–24) and group C (January 25–31). Universities pick one group for each department.
A department recruits in only one group, so departments of the same university can be in different groups.
Applicants submit one application per group, up to three in total. Interviews and practical exams take place within that group's period.
All applications, regardless of group, are submitted between January 4 and 7.

afterScore.title: After scores come out
items: Check your standard scores, percentiles and grades, and calculate converted scores using each university's subject weighting and how it reflects English and Korean history grades.
Check early admission results first: first-round results by December 18 and waitlist offers by December 29. If you are admitted early, you cannot apply in the regular round.
Build three applications by group, mixing safe, target and reach choices. Past admission results are available on Adiga and each university's admissions site.
Signing up for an integrated account with one application service (UWAY Apply or Jinhak Apply) lets you apply to universities on either service. Enter a refund account you actually use.

afterResult.title: After results: registering, withdrawing and refunds
items: First-round results come out by February 5, and registration runs February 10–12. Not registering in time counts as declining.
Waitlist offers go out February 13–17 in rank order. Website announcements run until 2 p.m.; from 2 to 6 p.m. offers are made individually, for example by phone, so answer your phone.

To switch to another university after a waitlist offer, first withdraw (request a refund) at the university where you registered, then register at the new one. Withdrawing promptly from places you will not take gives the next applicant a chance.
If you withdraw before the semester starts, your tuition is refunded in full (under the Regulation on University Tuition). Follow each admissions office's notice for how and when to withdraw.

addRecruit.title: Additional recruitment
items: Seats left after the regular waitlist are filled February 19–26. Notices appear after 6 p.m. on February 18, and applications, screening, offers and registration finish within 8 days.
Early admission admits and regular registrants cannot apply, unless they withdrew their regular registration by 4 p.m. on February 18.
Offers are due by 6 p.m. on February 26 and registration closes at 10 p.m. the same day. The schedule is short, so check notices right away.

items.q: How many regular admission applications can I submit?
items.a: One per group (A, B and C), up to three. Applying to two or more universities in the same group voids your admission. Industrial universities and junior colleges have no group limit, and special-act institutions such as the military academies, Korean National Police University and KAIST can be applied to separately.

items.q: If I was admitted in early admission but do not register, can I apply in the regular round?
items.a: No. Early admission admits, whether first round or waitlist, cannot apply in the regular or additional rounds regardless of registration. You also cannot give up an early admission waitlist rank.

items.q: When and what time do 2027 regular applications close?
items.a: The common window is January 4 (Mon) to 7 (Thu), 2027, and each university uses at least 3 of these days. Closing dates and times differ: Korea University (Seoul) closes January 6 at 6 p.m. Servers get busy on closing days, so apply early.

items.q: When are regular admission results and registration?
items.a: First-round results come out by February 5 (Fri), 2027, and registration runs February 10 (Wed) – 12 (Fri). Waitlist offers run February 13 (Sat) – 17 (Wed) until 6 p.m., and waitlist registration closes February 18 (Thu) at 10 p.m.

items.q: Do I get my tuition back if I withdraw?
items.a: If you withdraw before the semester starts, tuition is refunded in full. Request withdrawal (refund) on the admissions website, and when switching to another university after a waitlist offer, withdraw first and then register so it does not count as double registration.

items.q: Who can apply for additional recruitment?
items.a: Anyone except early admission admits and regular registrants. Regular registrants who withdrew by 4 p.m. on February 18 can apply. Additional recruitment runs February 19 (Fri) – 26 (Fri).

items.q: When do 2027 CSAT scores come out?
items.a: On December 11 (Fri), 2026. Once you have your scores, calculate converted scores for each university, shortlist candidates by group, and check early admission results (due by December 18) first.
